util

Class ProjectBuildInfo

  • java.lang.Object
    • util.ProjectBuildInfo

  • public final class ProjectBuildInfo
extends java.lang.Object
    Identifies the active JAR library file from which the current class is running. This utility obtains the file name and the last compilation date and time, effectively capturing the build date of the library.

    This class captures the JAR name accurately at runtime. However, if a JAR is not used (such as during IDE development), it assumes the name of the current running class instead.

      • getFileName

        public java.nio.file.Path getFileName()
        Returns the file name of the JAR library or the current running class resource. Unlike getFullPath(), this includes only the final name element and its extension, for example: MyLibrary.jar or MyClass.class.
        Returns:
        the file name as a Path object

      • getBuildDate

        public java.lang.String getBuildDate()
        Returns a human-readable string representation of the build date and time. The format used is dd/MM/yyyy @ hh:mm a, for example: 27/03/2026 @ 07:45 PM.
        Returns:
        the formatted build date string, or "Unknown" if the timestamp could not be determined

      • getFullBuildDate

        public java.util.Date getFullBuildDate()
        Returns the build date-time as a legacy Date object. This provides backwards compatibility with older APIs while representing the same point in time as the actual build resource.

        Note: While the internal state uses Instant precision, this method returns a value truncated to millisecond precision as required by the Date class.

        Returns:
        a Date object representing the last modification or compilation time of the resource

      • getShortFileName

        public java.nio.file.Path getShortFileName()
        Returns a concise identifier for the resource by extracting the filename and removing common extensions (.class or .jar) if present.
        Returns:
        a Path representing the normalized resource name

      • getInstance

        public static ProjectBuildInfo getInstance(java.lang.Class<?> currentClass)
        Resolves the physical resource (JAR or .class file) for the specified class and extracts its build metadata.

        This static factory method serves as the primary entry point for identifying the active resource location and capturing environmental details, such as the absolute file path and the last compilation timestamp.

        Parameters:
        currentClass - the class reference used to resolve the underlying resource location
        Returns:
        an initialised ProjectBuildInfo instance containing the resource identity and build metadata
        Throws:
        java.lang.NullPointerException - if the provided currentClass is null

      • readBuildInfo

        private void readBuildInfo(java.net.URL resource)
                    throws java.net.URISyntaxException,
                           java.io.IOException
        Internal helper to resolve the physical resource path and extract build metadata.

        If the URL points to a JAR file, it retrieves the entry's timestamp. If the URL points to a directory, it resolves the local .class file and extracts the filesystem modification time.

        Parameters:
        resource - the URL of the active class or JAR resource to be evaluated
        Throws:
        java.net.URISyntaxException - if the resource URL is malformed or cannot be converted to a valid URI
        java.io.IOException - if an I/O error occurs while accessing the JAR or filesystem resource

      • decodePath

        private java.lang.String decodePath(java.lang.String urlPath)
                             throws java.io.IOException
        Decodes a URL-encoded path string into a standard file system path. This method specifically handles the leading slash often prepended to absolute Windows paths by the ClassLoader, for example: converting /C:/ to C:/).
        Parameters:
        urlPath - the URL-encoded path string to be decoded
        Returns:
        the decoded file system path string
        Throws:
        java.io.IOException - if the decoding process fails or the encoding is unsupported

      • getJarManifestTimestamp

        private java.time.Instant getJarManifestTimestamp(java.lang.String jarPath)
                                           throws java.io.IOException
        Retrieves the build time-stamp from the META-INF/MANIFEST.MF entry within the specified JAR file.

        If the manifest entry cannot be obtained, the method resolves to the last modified time of the JAR file itself on the file system.

        Parameters:
        jarPath - the absolute file system path to the JAR resource
        Returns:
        an Instant representing the build time, accurate to the limits of the JAR/File System metadata
        Throws:
        java.io.IOException - if an I/O error occurs while accessing the JAR file or its entries
